pinProvenance.status: Previously established Chromium DEPS pin; not re-fetched in this six-file audit.

contentVerification: Nix-managed Node SHA-256 over exact returned UTF-8 bytes, with no normalization; SHA-1 of blob <byteLength> NUL plus bytes matches every connector-provided Git blob identity.

findings.finding: AllocationEvent charges only the terminal trace node using AddAllocation(size); AddAllocation increments its own size and count. Summing every node once therefore sums recorded allocation events, not inclusive ancestor totals or retained-object sizes.

Tracking start creates a fresh AllocationTracker; stop destroys it. Object movement updates address mappings and object-size updates affect the object map, without subtracting trace totals. The reviewed trace tree has no collection-based reset/decrement; script weak callbacks remove script metadata only.
Snapshot trace_node_fields names count and size; SerializeTraceNode emits allocation_count and allocation_size and recursively emits children. These are distinct from live heap node self_size.

Per-node total_size and allocation_count are unsigned with unchecked addition/increment. On a 32-bit-unsigned target ABI, each silently wraps modulo 2^32. JavaScript safe-integer validation of the serialized result cannot detect prior wrap. This audit does not prove a workload bound preventing overflow or a packaged-binary counter-width measurement.

Adding the first heap allocation tracker disables inline allocation when inline_new is enabled; disabling frees main-thread linear allocation areas. Removing the last tracker re-enables inline allocation. This is evidence of changed allocation machinery, not exhaustive proof of every JIT/slow/large/background/shared-heap path.

The inline allocator aligns requested size and either advances a linear allocation area or delegates failure to AllocateRawSlow. The slow-path implementation, large-object paths and generated JIT allocation code are outside this six-file audit; completeness is unresolved.

The tracker belongs to one profiler/heap and records addressed heap allocation events. This audit does not establish coverage of external ArrayBuffer/string backing stores, DOM/layout/native allocator traffic, other isolates/workers or all browser processes. Stack capture is bounded to 64 frames, so attribution can be truncated independently of accumulated event sizes.

conclusion: Pinned-source mechanism audit completed for these six files only. Cumulative trace events survive collection within one tracking session, subject to unchecked per-node overflow. Packaged-binary identity/coverage, exhaustive allocation hooks, workload bounds, backing stores and whole-browser aggregation remain unresolved. No acceptance metric or ceiling is established.
